summary: A harness.usage response_rollup series replicates its first reading, the last reading of each UTC hour once that hour is over, and its final totals when the seat ends, instead of every five minutes and at every turn end; the seat's host still reads its newest totals

replay.detail: Fewer harness.usage claims are written. A response_rollup reading after the series' first stays pending in the host's local observation log. It replicates when a later reading of the series falls in a later UTC hour (by observed_at_unix_ms), when a re-stamp of the resting seat arrives after its hour, or when the seat reports ended. Turn ends and the five-minute interval no longer replicate rollups. Context occupancy, cumulative and response readings keep the existing rules. Old claims are untouched.

schema.detail: No schema change: pending rollups use the existing local_latest_slots.pending_local_id.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and digests are unchanged. Retention already keeps the last rollup of each UTC hour (usage_series_keep), which is what now replicates.

compatibility.detail: Contract C2 of the db-breakup plan, approved: usage periods are exact to the hour. On the seat's host, st usage, /v1/usage, /v1/client/usage and the agent, mission and run cards fold the pending rollups too, so they stay exact. On other members they lag by up to about an hour, and a period boundary inside an hour reads that hour's previous snapshot. Per-response detail is in OTLP. No claim kind, field, wire or CLI shape changes; an older node keeps replicating rollups on its old schedule, and every node reads both.

downtime.detail: No restart beyond the normal upgrade; no migration or backfill.

recovery.detail: No data recovery is needed. Reverting replicates each pending rollup at its seat's next turn end or interval; the readings stay in each host's local observation log meanwhile.
